dublinCore.title: Five Levels of Intelligent Textbooks
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Intelligent textbooks
Educational technology
Adaptive learning
AI in education
Student data privacy
dublinCore.description: Interactive stair-step diagram of the five levels of intelligent textbooks, from static (Level 1) to autonomous AI (Level 5). Hover over, tap or press 1 to 5 to read what each level includes; a dashed rectangle marks Levels 3 to 5 as highly regulated.
relation: Instructor's Guide: The Five Levels of Intelligent Textbooks

learningObjectives: Identify the five levels of intelligent textbooks in order from the stair-step diagram: Static, Interactive Content, Adaptive, Chatbot Integration and Autonomous AI
Distinguish Level 2 interactive content such as search, hyperlinks and embedded MicroSims from Level 3 adaptivity, which adjusts content from learner input and performance
Explain why Level 3 adaptive textbooks require concept graph traversal and data management systems that Level 2 textbooks do not
Evaluate the student-privacy considerations that arise once a textbook records learner data, using the dashed Highly Regulated Textbooks rectangle around Levels 3 to 5
Classify a given textbook or course website into one of the five levels from its interactive and personalization features
prerequisites: Experience reading a digital textbook or course website
Basic awareness of what a chatbot is

misconceptions.misconception: A higher level is simply a better textbook for every purpose
misconceptions.correction: Each level adds capability but also implementation requirements and privacy considerations; Level 1 remains suitable where interaction is not needed, and Level 5 is still aspirational
misconceptions.evidence: Hover over Level 1 (suitable for simple content delivery), Level 3 (requires data management systems and raises privacy considerations) and Level 5 (remains aspirational)

misconceptions.misconception: Adding videos, quizzes or MicroSims makes a textbook adaptive
misconceptions.correction: Those features belong to Level 2; a textbook becomes adaptive (Level 3) only when it adjusts content to the individual learner's input and performance
misconceptions.evidence: Compare the Level 2 description (search, hyperlinks, videos, quizzes) with the Level 3 description (personalized learning pathways, concept mastery)

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Stair-step diagram of the five levels of intelligent textbooks: Level 1 static textbooks, Level 2 interactive content, Level 3 adaptive textbooks, Level 4 chatbot integration and Level 5 autonomous AI. Levels 3 to 5 are enclosed in a dashed rectangle labelled Highly Regulated Textbooks. Selecting a level, by hovering, tapping or pressing the keys 1 to 5, shows its description.

visualElements.description: Five stacked rectangles forming a staircase, Level 1 (red) at the bottom to Level 5 (gold) at the top, each labelled with its level name; the selected level has a blue border
Dashed red rectangle around Levels 3, 4 and 5 with the label Highly Regulated Textbooks
Description of the selected level below the staircase, or a prompt to hover, tap or press 1 to 5 when no level is selected

instructionalStrategies: Compare adjacent levels by hovering over them in turn
Classify familiar textbooks and course sites onto the staircase and justify each placement
extensions: Place a textbook you use on the staircase and list the features that put it there
Draft a short data-privacy policy for a Level 3 textbook
